newsitem.title: UK: Bearish Bradys await U.S. jobs data for bearing.
newsitem.headline: Bearish Bradys await U.S. jobs data for bearing.

text.p: The U.S. employment report for March kept an airtight lid on Brady market activity on Friday as players awaited an indication of possible interest rate moves from the Federal Reserve, dealers said.
"Trade is very thin, we've literally seen one Minfin seller," a Brady trader said.
According to a Reuters poll, U.S. economists forecast U.S. payrolls rose by 196,000 in March, down from 339,000 new jobs in February.
There is some speculation of another 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"If it's a bad number today (Friday) we could see the market drop one point this afternoon, but if its a good number we could see a one-and-a-half-point rally," a dealer said.
Overnight reports from New York said in spite of the Standard & Poor's Corp upgrade of Argentina and Brazil, nervousness ahead of the key economic data muted reaction.
"The upgrades did not lead to buying," a Brady dealer said. "The market tone is bearish at present."
He said the Brady market this week had taken its direction from the recent U.S. equity and bond market slip rather than being lead by emerging market sovereign fundamentals.
